b1-37-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Safe Arrival
b1-37-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos's sister Ana has just arrived in Budapest on the evening train, and you meet her at the station.
b1-37-01.prompt: Welcome Ana: say you hope she has had a good trip and that you are glad she has arrived.
cues: Say you hope she has had a good trip
Say you are glad she has arrived
b1-37-01.target: Espero que hayas tenido un buen viaje. Me alegro de que hayas llegado bien.
b1-37-01.english: I hope you have had a good trip. I am glad you have arrived safely.
b1-37-01.canDo: I can form the present perfect subjunctive with haya + participio.

b1-37-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Good News
b1-37-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg tells you that she has passed the last exam of the term at her university.
b1-37-02.prompt: Tell Meg how you feel: you are glad she has passed, and it is a relief.
cues: Say you are glad she has passed the exam
Say what a relief it is
b1-37-02.target: Me alegro de que hayas aprobado el examen. ¡Qué alivio que hayas terminado!
b1-37-02.english: I am glad you have passed the exam. What a relief that you have finished!
b1-37-02.canDo: I can say how I feel about something that has happened, using the present perfect subjunctive.

b1-37-03.title: Communicative Challenge: I Doubt It
b1-37-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says that your sister Kaylee has already sent the family photos, but you have not received anything.
b1-37-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that you doubt it and that you don't think she has done it yet.
cues: Say you doubt Kaylee has sent the photos
Say you don't think she has done it yet
b1-37-03.target: Dudo que Kaylee haya mandado las fotos. No creo que lo haya hecho todavía.
b1-37-03.english: I doubt Kaylee has sent the photos. I don't think she has done it yet.
b1-37-03.canDo: I can doubt or deny that something has happened, using the present perfect subjunctive.

b1-37-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Dinner After the Report
b1-37-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks when you can go out for dinner. You still have to finish a report for your office.
b1-37-04.prompt: Tell Meg you will go out with her as soon as you have finished the report.
cues: Say you will go out for dinner
Say what you have to finish first
b1-37-04.target: Saldremos a cenar en cuanto haya terminado el informe.
b1-37-04.english: We will go out for dinner as soon as I have finished the report.
b1-37-04.canDo: I can say that an action will be finished before another one, using cuando or en cuanto + present perfect subjunctive.

b1-37-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Exam
b1-37-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg has an exam tomorrow morning and you phone her in the evening.
b1-37-05.prompt: Tell Meg you hope she has rested today and that the exam goes well tomorrow.
cues: Say you hope she has rested today
Say you hope the exam goes well tomorrow
b1-37-05.target: Espero que hayas descansado hoy y que el examen salga bien mañana.
b1-37-05.english: I hope you have rested today and that the exam goes well tomorrow.
b1-37-05.canDo: I can choose between the present subjunctive and the present perfect subjunctive.

b1-37-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: An Evening at Home
b1-37-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos has just come home from a long day at his office in Budapest.
b1-37-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos you are glad he has come home, and that you will watch a film with him as soon as he has eaten.
cues: Say you are glad he has come home
Say what you will do when he has eaten
b1-37-consolidation.target: Me alegro de que hayas vuelto a casa. Veremos una película en cuanto hayas cenado.
b1-37-consolidation.english: I am glad you have come home. We will watch a film as soon as you have had dinner.
b1-37-consolidation.canDo: I can use the present perfect subjunctive for feelings, doubts and future completion.
